title: Sustainable Shopping Statistics: 2027 Guide
summary: Explore sustainable shopping statistics and trends to understand the current state of buyer behavior and how to appeal to eco-conscious consumers.
body_markdown:
Sustainable shopping refers to the environmental practices and considerations that brands and consumers embrace in an effort to do less harm to the planet. For a business, responding to growing consumer interest in environmental sustainability and personal well-being can impact its success in the marketplace.


According to data from the[NYU Stern Center for Sustainable Business and Circana](https://www.stern.nyu.edu/experience-stern/faculty-research/opinion/demystifying-say-do-gap-sustainable-product-purchases) , sustainably marketed[consumer packaged goods (CPG)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/cpg) have grown 4.9 times faster than conventional products since 2013. Over the same period, sustainable products were responsible for nearly 45% of all CPG market growth despite making up just a quarter of the market in 2025.


Here are more of the latest sustainable shopping statistics around key trends and initiatives taking shape to meet consumer demand for eco-friendly alternatives.


## What is sustainable shopping?


Sustainable shopping means shopping with a mindful eye toward consumption and considering the environmental or social impact of a purchase. For consumers, that means choosing[sustainable brands](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sustainable-brands) that seek to minimize environmental harm, as well as building more sustainable habits like buying less or secondhand and contributing to a circular economy by keeping items in use and out of landfills for as long as possible.


For businesses, sustainable shopping practices look like using sustainable materials, ethical supply chains, and environmental fulfillment methods that reduce the carbon emissions of shipping.

## Sustainable shopping statistics

The following statistics help paint a portrait of modern conscious consumerism. Brands looking to prioritize sustainability and help build a more sustainable future can learn from the data, organized by category:


### Consumer demand


Consumer demand for—and curiosity about—the positive impact of their purchases continues to shape sustainable shopping. “People really do want to support sustainable brands,”[Sabai Design](https://sabai.design/) founder Phantila Phataraprasit says on[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sabai-design-sustainability) , “and those companies are growing faster than their counterparts.” Here are some supporting figures:


-


Per[Capital One Shopping](https://capitaloneshopping.com/research/eco-conscious-consumer-statistics/) , consumers spent an estimated $230 billion on eco-friendly products in 2025, up 12.5% year over year.


-


A 2026[YouGov survey](https://yougov.com/en-us/articles/54722-consumer-concern-americans-increasingly-concerned-about-ingredient-safety-in-everyday-products) found that 78% of Americans are concerned about the safety of ingredients in products such as food, cosmetics, and personal care items, and 39% have switched to products perceived as more “natural” or “clean.”


-


According to[The Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/style/fashion/cotton-fiber-pfas-47042bd2) , the share of global Google searches for “100% cotton” in 2026 roughly quadrupled from the same search term in 2025.


-


Research by[Bain Consumer Lab](https://www.bain.com/insights/for-consumers-sustainability-isnt-gone-but-it-is-changing-ceo-sustainability-guide-2026/) found that 48% of consumers who use AI say they use it to help live more sustainably; 43% said they use it to determine whether a product is healthy and 38% to get eco-friendly product recommendations.


### Generational differences


A paradox has emerged between older generations and Gen Z and younger millennial consumers, who consistently demonstrate the largest desire for sustainable, eco-friendly purchases but are one of the largest purchasing groups powering fast fashion sites like SHEIN and Temu—a “say-do” gap driven by affordability. Here are some trends:


-


According to[Statista](http://statista.com/statistics/1626151/shoppers-who-prefer-buying-from-sustainable-brands-us/) , 60% of millennial and 58% of Gen Z consumers in the US prioritize buying from brands with sustainable and ethical practices, compared to 43% and 37% of Gen X and baby boomers, respectively.


-


In a study by[Opeepl](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/63d132d5514fc03856edc10f/t/6a4e380d77a00770ad4ffeee/1783511053533/Gaining+the+Edge+-+Decoding+Youth+Trends+in+2026+compressed.pdf) , younger consumers (defined as between 15 and 30) define “sustainable consumption” as recycling or reselling items they no longer use, and buying products made from recycled or upcycled materials.


-


In a[Mastercard report](https://www.mastercard.com/content/dam/mccom/shared/news-and-trends/insights/2026/the-new-era-of-conscious-consumption/The%20next%20era%20of%20conscious%20consumption_Mastercard.pdf) , 61% of shoppers under 30 said they’d rather spend their money on environmentally friendly products than reduce the number of products they buy overall.


-


While Gen Z consumers show higher purchase intent around sustainability,[a Savanta report](https://www.research-live.com/article/news/baby-boomers-more-likely-to-shop-sustainably-than-gen-z-finds-savanta-study/id/5131553) in the UK found that boomers were more likely to engage in sustainable shopping behaviors than younger generations, with 75% using reusable bags, 44% buying loose goods, 52% buying produce in season, and 40% only buying recyclable packaging.


### Greenwashing and transparency


[Greenwashing](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-greenwashing) is the term for deceiving consumers by claiming a product or business is more sustainable or environmentally responsible than it truly is. It can tarnish consumer trust and brand perception. One of the best ways to protect that trust is by sharing information about sourcing, manufacturing, and environmental certifications like[1% for the Planet](https://www.onepercentfortheplanet.org/) ,[Cradle to Cradle (C2C)](https://c2ccertified.org/the-standard) , or[OEKO-TEX](https://www.oeko-tex.com/en/) , among others.


“It’s very easy for companies to throw out terms like ‘sustainability’ and ‘organic,’”[Bedi Studios](https://bedistudios.com/) Founder Inder Bedi says on *[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/bedi-studios-second-chance-for-sustainable-fashion)* . “I think that’s one of the positive things we’re seeing in 2026 versus 1995: consumers are actually asking, ‘What does that mean? What does that actually entail?’ To drive the industry to be more accountable, we need to see more of that.” Recent customer data confirms that greenwashing is a growing concern:


-


According to[Capital One Shopping](https://capitaloneshopping.com/research/eco-conscious-consumer-statistics/) , 23% of consumers want to buy more eco-friendly products, but don’t always believe brands’ sustainability claims.


-


As of September 2026, the EU’s[Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition (ECGT)](https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/policies/consumers/consumer-protection-policy/empowering-consumers-green-transition_en) directive strictly prohibits brands from using vague terms like “eco-friendly,” “green,” or “sustainable” unless they can provide specific, certified proof.


### Impact


For consumers, sustainable choices signal a sense of environmental responsibility, as well as a regard for personal health and safety. For brands and businesses, proof of sustainable practices and products builds trust both between customer and brand and between customer and manufacturer.


“At Sabai, sustainability means looking at the entire picture,” Phantila says. “Whether it’s addressing the amount of waste, or addressing the actual materials that go into furniture products, or looking at the longevity of products.” Here are some recent findings on the environmental impacts of ecommerce:


-


In the US alone, over[12 million tons of furniture waste](https://www.epa.gov/facts-and-figures-about-materials-waste-and-recycling/durable-goods-product-specific-data) is created every single year. Eighty percent of that goes directly to landfills.


-


Only[46% of global brands](https://capitaloneshopping.com/research/eco-conscious-consumer-statistics/) invest in post-consumer recyclable programs.


-


[Shopify’s 2025 Climate Report](https://cdn.shopify.com/static/sustainability/climate-report/Shopify-2025-Climate-Report.pdf) finds that since its launch in 2022, sellers using Shopify’s[Planet](https://apps.shopify.com/planet) app have generated 73 million carbon-neutral orders, addressing more than 52,000 tonnes of shipping emissions and contributing $3 million to carbon removal.


### Materials


The fashion industry, one of the world’s largest contributors to emissions and annual waste, is experiencing a recent surge in interest around natural fabrics and alternative materials, ethical and sustainable practices, and efforts to improve animal welfare and fair labor practices.


For brands, consumer demand for high-quality eco-friendly or ethically sourced products can also result in lower return rates. Home goods brand[Goodee](https://www.goodeeworld.com/) , for example, has a return rate of 4.5% (compared to the 17% ecommerce industry average). Founders Byron and Dexter Peart attribute this to the intense curation of their global catalog and the values-driven shopping experience of their customers.


“We believe that people actually do want to make a better choice, but they just don’t necessarily know how to,” Byron says on[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/goodee-curating-purpose-and-profits) . “If you put 10,000 products in front of them, how would anyone even know where to start, or how to make a good choice? I think it’s incumbent on us to really help the customer with their buying decisions.” Helping customers make higher-quality, more sustainable choices, he argues, is better for everyone involved.


Here are recent trends on materials in the clothing and beauty industries:


-


Per Textile Exchange’s[2025 Materials Market Report](https://textileexchange.org/knowledge-center/reports/materials-market-report-2025/) , global fiber production increased to 132 million tonnes in 2024. Petroleum-derived polyester remains the most widely produced fiber, making up 59% of total global fiber output, 88% of which is fossil-based.


-


According to[The Business of Fashion](https://www.businessoffashion.com/articles/sustainability/why-consumers-ditching-polyester-for-natural-fibres/) , searches for “natural material clothing” have spiked by around 850% in the US, while specific queries like “is viscose a natural fiber?” or “what is viscose?” and other related searches have climbed by more than 5,000% over the past five years, signaling a growing consumer appetite for understanding.


-


A report by the[National Sanitation Foundation (NSF)](https://nsfinternational.widen.net/s/ccj6qzb8rf/nsf-consumer-personal-care-whitepaper-2025) found that 74% of consumers consider organic ingredients important in beauty and personal care products; younger consumers ages 18 to 29 place higher importance on organic ingredients at 86%, compared to older consumers ages 60 to 75 at 59%.


### Packaging


[Sustainable packaging](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sustainable-packaging-and-shipping-solutions) includes eco-friendly mailers, product refills, reusable packaging, or new solutions like the biodegradable Vivomer packaging used by skincare brand[Sonsie](https://www.instagram.com/p/DQmy0jjERkN/?img_index=2) , as well as new gadgets like[Aerflo](https://aerflo.co/) , a portable carbonation device that eliminates the need for wasteful packaging in the first place.


The 5majority of what consumers interact with every day and do their part to recycle is highly unsustainable packaging, like plastic waste and multi-material components that are too difficult for recycling facilities to sort and break down.


“It’s no secret that single-use is not a sustainable way to move forward into the next century. We can’t just keep making one-off things, pretend we’re going to recycle them, and throw them in the ocean,” Aerflo Cofounder Buzz Wiggins says on[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/aerflo-shaking-up-the-beverage-industry) . “Everyone thinks that as long as it gets in that bin, it’s all good. That’s not the case.”


These figures on packaging and sustainability indicate the scale of the issue and recent trends:


-


According to a[Smithers report](https://www.smithers.com/resources/2025/december/packaging-waste-outpacing-global-capacity) , global waste generated from packaging reached an estimated 434.5 million tonnes in 2025.


-


When asked by[McKinsey](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/packaging-and-paper/our-insights/sustainability-in-packaging-2025-inside-the-minds-of-global-consumers) , consumers overwhelmingly placed the burden of responsibility for sustainable packaging adoption on brand owners and packaging producers, not consumers themselves.


-


A[Packaging World survey](https://www.packworld.com/leaders-new/business-drivers-specialty/sustainability/video/22947559/survey-cost-tops-list-of-biggest-barriers-to-sustainable-packaging) found that 78% of CPG brands cite cost as the biggest barrier to adopting eco-friendly packaging.


-


The[compostable packaging industry](https://www.thebusinessresearchcompany.com/report/compostable-packaging-global-market-report) is projected to reach $140 billion in 2030, growing at a[compound annual growth rate (CAGR)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-calculate-growth-rate) of 7.1%, driven by the increasing availability of bio-based raw materials.


-


Biodegradable food boxes, in particular, are one rapidly growing segment. According to[DHR research](https://datahorizzonresearch.com/biodegradable-lunch-box-market-25347) , the market for eco-friendly food storage solutions was valued at $50 million in 2024 and is anticipated to reach around $100.6 million in 2033.


### Pricing


In several reports concerning sustainable shopping behaviors, consumers say they’re willing to pay more for better environmental outcomes, but cost of living and inflation are making those values-driven purchases harder to justify (and making the cheaper, convenient, less sustainable options more appealing).


“Studies show that younger generations are willing to pay more of a premium for these products that align with their values. We wanted to create a solution that spoke to those values but also took accessibility and budget into account,” Sabai Design’s Phantila says. “How do we provide solutions that make an impact, but also meet our community and our customers where they are in terms of what they can afford?” Here are some statistics on how pricing impacts consumers’ sustainability choices:


-


According to the[PwC 2024 Voice of the Consumer Survey](https://www.pwc.com/gx/en/news-room/press-releases/2024/pwc-2024-voice-of-consumer-survey.html) , more than 80% of consumers say they are willing to pay more for sustainably produced or sourced goods.


-


The same PwC report found that those consumers were willing to pay almost 10% more on average for goods that met specific environmental criteria, like items that were locally sourced, made from recycled or eco-friendly materials, or produced in a supply chain with a lower carbon footprint.


-


Research from[Simon-Kucher](https://www.simon-kucher.com/en/insights/how-make-sustainability-growth-driver) found that 78% of consumers consider sustainability a top-five purchasing criterion in at least one category, but pricing 10% to 30% above conventional competitors often restricts sales to niche buyers, or “green champions.” Achieving mass adoption requires closing the price gap or marketing specific benefits like long-term cost savings or durability.


### Resale


Along with secondhand shopping and thrifting, many consumers now turn to dedicated online resale marketplaces to more easily source and sell used items. Some brands, like Sabai Design’s[Revive](https://sabai.design/pages/sabai-revive) program and Bedi Studios’[Second Life](https://bedistudios.com/pages/second-life?srsltid=AU7gw4XhfG32c5H9selu40LqdokG3kFhmL-qUjNP1PeD5aZ8yhO--R-e) , have embraced the practice by launching their own circular programs in-house, either with a brand-specific[resale](https://www.shopify.com/blog/resale) market or by offering to refurbish and sell used items at a discount through their store platform. Here’s what recent resale data shows:


-


The global secondhand apparel market is projected to reach $393 billion by 2030, growing twice as fast as the overall apparel market, according to ThredUp’s[2026 Resale Report](https://www.thredup.com/resale?srsltid=AU7gw4W258T_dGJbUr4rRpsOMrejUIrYmBCRF2xFzDk8EeZqV1Tion2v) .


-


According to a[Mastercard survey](https://www.mastercard.com/content/dam/mccom/shared/news-and-trends/insights/2026/the-new-era-of-conscious-consumption/The%20next%20era%20of%20conscious%20consumption_Mastercard.pdf) , 20% of Gen Z and 18% of millennial consumers say they consider a product’s resale value before making a new purchase.


-


According to[McKinsey](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/consumer-packaged-goods/our-insights/state-of-consumer) , 82% of global consumers say they are using items longer before replacing them, 69% attempt to repair products rather than throw them out, and 68% say they are actively trying to reduce waste overall.


-


According to Mastercard,[56% of consumers](https://www.mastercard.com/content/dam/mccom/shared/news-and-trends/insights/2026/the-new-era-of-conscious-consumption/The%20next%20era%20of%20conscious%20consumption_Mastercard.pdf) who seek out secondhand products are driven by their values—specifically, to reduce waste and support a circular economy—over cost.


## Sustainable shopping statistics FAQ


### What is sustainable shopping?


Sustainable shopping refers both to the buying of eco-friendly products from brands that prioritize sustainable materials and ethical sourcing, as well as an overall shopping philosophy that prioritizes longevity, health, and reduction of waste in purchasing decisions.


### Why does Gen Z care about sustainability?


Gen Z cares about sustainability because they have come of age in the era of climate change, a threat that directly impacts their future quality of life. Research from[GlobeScan and BBMG](https://globescan.com/2025/05/21/insight-of-the-week-gen-z-climate-impact/) found that 73% of Gen Z respondents were “extremely worried” about current and future harm to the planet, while 38% felt anxious all or most of the time about environmental instability.


### What are some examples of sustainable shopping brands?


Examples of brands’ sustainability efforts include Blueland selling dry tablets for common household cleaners instead of encouraging consumers to buy new plastic bottles; Bedi Studios, which uses upcycled materials to create its durable outerwear; and skincare brand Sonsie, which uses bio-based packaging, is certified plastic-negative, and prioritizes sustainable initiatives.
